newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has asked the law minister to frame a law providing capital punishment for abusing and repressing women.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Sunday called for building up a mass movement against what he called massive infiltration of Indian products into the country.
Europena Community report on cotton development in Bangladesh has praised the quality of cotton produced here.
The supply of urea fertiliser across the country was satiafactory and prices were eight percent lower than the corresponding period of last year, said a government handout on Sunday.
Finance Minister S A M S Kibria on Sunday described newspaper reports on country's economic position as "negative and baseless", and said economic indicators had improved over the months.
The Faysal Islamic Bank of Bahrain, a subsidiary of Switzerland-based Dar Al Maal Al Islami, has decided to set up a branch in Dhaka.
Islamic Development Bank (IDB) has decided to provide $10 million loan for rural electrification project in Bangladesh.
Four Bangladeshi companies have applied for launching private airlines after the government opened up the domestic sky for private sector aircrafts having upto 80 seats.
